issues.title: Cut per-row VARCHAR-key overhead in radix hash aggregate (sink/repartition/combine)
issues.hypothesis: Measured with EXPLAIN ANALYZE at 8 threads. q16 as written: HASH_GROUP_BY 0.65-0.70s CPU, 255-309 ms total. The same query with the VARCHAR group key p_type replaced by hash(p_type) (BIGINT): HASH_GROUP_BY 0.23s, 169 ms total. With substr(p_type,1,12) (an inlined VARCHAR, 5x fewer groups) it is still 0.56s. A plain GROUP BY on brand,type,size,suppkey (1.18M groups, which is the distinct phase) costs 0.85s on its own. So the overhead is in the VARCHAR layout path itself (layout !AllConstant) and does not depend on heap pointer chasing or on group count. It is mostly in the high-cardinality first (distinct) phase. Candidates I found by reading the code: (a) with radix_bits >= UNPARTITIONED_RADIX_BITS_THRESHOLD (3), and the sink starts at that with 8 threads, every Abandon() (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:129-138) runs unpartitioned_data->Repartition into partitioned_data. That is a second full copy of every row. For heap layouts it also copies heap data and recomputes pointers, and a near-unique HT abandons every ~21.8k rows. (b) PartitionedTupleData::Append (partitioned_tuple_data.cpp:55-88) runs ComputeHeapSizes plus a per-partition heap BuildBufferSpace on each chunk. (c) The finalize Combine (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:883) re-gathers and re-scatters all strings. Fixing whichever dominates should move VARCHAR-key aggregation toward the fixed-width cost.
issues.plan: 1) Measure first, then fix. Add temporary timers (or rebuild variants) around these phases for the q16 shape (the variant with hash(p_type) is the fast reference): GroupedAggregateHashTable::FindOrCreateGroups / partitioned append, Abandon() -> unpartitioned_data->Repartition, the RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize -> ht->Combine path, and Scan. 2) Fix the dominant phase. Preferred if (a) dominates: for layouts that are not AllConstant, skip the unpartitioned staging and append directly into partitioned_data. Do this by not using the UNPARTITIONED_RADIX_BITS_THRESHOLD path when the layout has heap columns, gated in GroupedAggregateHashTable where unpartitioned_data is chosen (aggregate_hashtable.cpp ~line 60-140 and the FindOrCreateGroups append site). Alternatively make Repartition for heap layouts reuse the existing heap blocks. If (b) dominates: skip ComputeHeapSizes/heap buffer work for chunks whose VARCHAR values are all inlined. If (c) dominates: report the findings without forcing a fix. 3) Remove the timers and verify with dbe-tool bench.
issues.expected_gain: q16 10-30%. The hash(p_type) experiment bounds the attainable gain at ~85 ms of ~255 ms if VARCHAR-key aggregation were as cheap as fixed-width.
issues.generality: Any GROUP BY or count(DISTINCT) with string keys and medium-to-high group cardinality on multiple threads. This is very common (TPC-H q10/q13/q16/q18-style, string dimension keys). Possible slowdowns: skipping unpartitioned staging may cost cache misses when partitions are many and rows wide. Gate it on heap layouts only and check that low-cardinality string group-bys do not regress.
issues.risk: Medium. Aggregate HT internals with heap-pointer invariants (pin states, heap pointer recompute) can cause subtle corruption. Correctness is checked on hidden queries, so keep the change minimal and run the aggregate tests. Risk of no clear fix if the cost is spread across phases. If so, report the per-phase breakdown.

dispatch: Cut per-row VARCHAR-key overhead in radix hash aggregate (sink/repartition/combine)
output.memory:
## Memory (gen1 round2)

### Workload
- Only template q16: partsupp JOIN part (filtered: brand<>, type NOT LIKE prefix, size IN 8 consts) + NOT IN (supplier LIKE) mark join, GROUP BY brand,type,size count(DISTINCT suppkey). ~27.8k groups, ~1.18M rows into the agg. Bench ~174-180 ms.
- Round-1 time split (EXPLAIN ANALYZE totals): join only with count(*) 82 ms; adding GROUP BY with plain count 178 ms; with count(DISTINCT) ~222 ms.
- Profile operator cumulative CPU: HASH_GROUP_BY 0.47-0.70 s, inner HASH_JOIN 0.17-0.20 s, partsupp scan with BF 0.16-0.21 s, part scan 0.07-0.10 s (emits 1.86M rows; the IN filter is only optional and is applied by a MARK join).

### KEY FINDING round 2: VARCHAR group key is the dominant cost
- Same q16 with p_type -> hash(p_type) as the group key: HASH_GROUP_BY 0.23 s vs 0.65 s, total 169 ms vs 255 ms.
- substr(p_type,1,12) (an inlined VARCHAR, 5.5k groups): still 0.56 s. So the cost is the VARCHAR/heap layout path itself, not heap pointer chasing and not group count.
- Plain GROUP BY brand,type,size,suppkey (1.18M groups = the distinct phase alone): 0.85 s. So the high-cardinality distinct phase dominates.
- Suspects: Abandon() -> unpartitioned_data->Repartition (radix_bits >= UNPARTITIONED_RADIX_BITS_THRESHOLD = 3) is a double copy per row. Also ComputeHeapSizes/BuildBufferSpace per partition, and the finalize Combine re-scatter.
- R2 dispatched: "Cut per-row VARCHAR-key overhead in radix hash aggregate". It measures the phases first, then fixes the top one.

### Codebase facts
- Radix aggregate HT (src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp): with >2 threads the sink capacity is 32768 (resize threshold 21845). The HT is Abandon()ed when full. DecideAdaptation runs only after ADAPTIVITY_THRESHOLD = 1M rows per thread. MAXIMUM_FINAL_SINK_RADIX_BITS = 8. Row width thresholds 32/64 reduce max bits.
- GroupedAggregateHashTable (aggregate_hashtable.cpp): radix_bits >= 3 uses unpartitioned_data staging, repartitioned on Abandon/AcquirePartitionedData. Combine(TupleDataCollection&) at ~line 883 re-runs FindOrCreateGroups on the scanned rows.
- The finalize path: RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize (radix ~line 853) creates an HT sized to the partition count and Combines into it.
- count(DISTINCT) path (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp ~648-754): sinks only the distinct radix table (keys = groups + distinct col). HashAggregateDistinctFinalizeTask scans the distinct radix table via GetData and Sinks into the main table_data, then the main table finalizes.
- Compressed materialization: p_brand (8 chars) -> uhugeint, p_type (25 chars) stays VARCHAR, p_size -> utinyint. Strings are compressed only when max length <= 16.
- Perfect HJ gate: perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp CanDoPerfectHashJoin, MAX_BUILD_SIZE = 1048576 range, INNER only.
- InClauseRewriter: IN lists with >= 6 constants become a MARK join against a COLUMN_DATA_SCAN.
- dbe-tool: no perf profiler, no pipes. Use `dbe-tool sql "EXPLAIN ANALYZE ..."` for variant timing. Rewriting the query (e.g. hash() of a key) is a cheap way to bisect costs.

### Experiments
- E0001 early HT grow (retired): ~3% only. Abandon thrashing itself is only ~5 ms, and the 2.0 dedup-ratio test is wrong for early checks.

### Backlog ideas (ranked)
1. (dispatched R2) VARCHAR-key aggregate overhead.
2. Perfect HJ for sparse-bounded range (build 296k, range 2M, density ~1/7). Join + probe-side scan ~0.4 s CPU. Expected 5-10%.
3. Enforce the IN-list filter in the scan instead of the mark join (small, 2-4%).
4. Distinct HT for near-unique data: early SkipLookups (risky).

### Prior-run notes (other workloads, see MEMORY index): perfect HJ / large perfect HA gave ~20% on q13. FSST decode laziness etc. are not directly applicable here.
